title: raw/segments.json (written by the recorder, read by the packager)
description: One entry per video segment (a clip between pauses / restarts), in recording order. Written atomically after every segment stop, while recording (about every 10 s, the current segment with in_progress true) and when the recording stops, so a crashed session can still be packaged. Segment mp4s are fragmented MP4; the packager remuxes them into clip.mp4.

frames.description: Per-frame sidecar: [frame_index_in_segment, wall_clock_ms]. Duplicate-padded slots carry their nominal slot time (t0 + slot * 1000 / fps); the capture time of the frame they repeat is in duplicate_runs.

duplicate_runs.description: Runs of duplicate-padded slots (the encoder repeated the previous frame because no new capture arrived in time): [first_slot, last_slot, content_wall_ms], where content_wall_ms is the capture wall time (sync latency subtracted, like frames) of the frame the slots repeat. Slots are frame indexes in this segment; at most 5000 runs are kept.

duplicate_runs_dropped.description: Runs not listed in duplicate_runs because its limit was reached (absent when 0).

output_size.description: Encoded video size [width, height] of this segment after the even-size crop (an odd capture width or height is cropped by 1 px); null when unknown. Every segment of a recording has the same size.

finalized.description: FFmpeg exited 0 after EOF/'q'. false: the packager probes the file and fits frames to its decodable frames.

returncode.description: FFmpeg exit code (null while running or unknown).

broken.description: Nothing decodable: frames is empty and the packager skips the segment (its time becomes a gap).

in_progress.description: Still recording when this file was written (crash recovery): the packager probes the file like finalized false.
